Answer: C
Reason: Figure 1 shows a normal chest X-ray, while Figure 4 demonstrates a new tubular opacity (mucoid impaction) with surrounding hyperlucency in the left upper lobe; among the choices, option C is the only one that correctly identifies the classic radiographic triad of congenital bronchial atresia (tubular opacity + hyperlucent area), even though the "unchanged" descriptor contradicts the visible progression from a normal baseline.
